title: How much rests on each kind of evidence
question: How many of the groups above, and how much City money, rest on firm records, and how much on a shared address or surname?
finding: Of 300 sets of differently named City payees, 99 rest on a record that names the owner, the licensed person or the relationship (tiers 1 to 3; $1.23 billion paid under second and later names), 2 on an address plus a telephone or named owner (tier 4; $407,543), and 199 are address-only or surname leads (tiers 5 and 6; $366.7 million to the smaller side of each pair). Within tier 3, 23 groups ($764.7 million under second and later names) are nonprofits and the related organizations they declare on their own tax returns. Beyond payees, the groups file holds 410 groups with two or more names of interest and 326 address leads.
how: Every set from the first screen is counted once under the weakest tier needed to hold its payee names together. "Paid under second and later names" is the group’s City payments less its largest payee, so a parent paid under one name counts nothing. For tiers 5 and 6 each row is a pair, the money shown is what the smaller side received, and a payee in several pairs is counted in each. "All groups" also counts groups whose names of interest are bidders, contract team members, licence holders or grant applicants.
limits: The tiers measure the kind of record, not the likelihood of anything improper: a tier 1 group is certainly one owner and almost always an ordinary corporate family. Tier 6 produced 0 pair(s) because personal names are never used to join records here, so sole owners enter only through a registered trade name. Address tiers leave out 448 addresses that hold more owners than the stated limit (listed in droppedAddresses). What would move a row from a lead to a record is in toConfirm.
